title: Early WIP of a fantasy siege incremental roguelike . can you tell what's going on at a glance, and what feels off?
author: PoloteNewt
selftext:
>Hey everyone! still very much a work in progress and just looking for honest gut reactions and advice before I go deeper.  
>  
>You build walls, fuse elemental towers, and recruit autonomous squads around your Keep. When a siege eventually overwhelms you, your garrison stays intact. you bank Soul Shards from the run, roll nodes on an astrolabe skill web( 2 min in video) , pick a subclass, and push into harder tiers/maps.  
>  
>Full transparency: it's just me working on this, and I've been using AI tools (coding assistance + PixelLab sprites) to help me get the systems on screen so I can iterate on the actual loop and UI.  
>  
>Mostly hoping for blunt feedback on:  
>  
>  
>  
>  
Thank you all for any input!

comments.author: stolenyourgf
comments.body: Fun loop! What reads least clearly at a glance is units vs. background. A few things that help a lot with PixelLab sprites: lock everything to one palette (even 16–24 colors) so towers, squads and enemies feel like one set; give units a 1px dark outline or darker rim so they pop off the terrain; keep the pixel scale consistent (no mixed-res or rotated pixels); and put enemies in a different hue family from your units so a siege reads instantly.

comments.author: YYY003003
comments.body: Classic early vibecoded game. The pixel densities of your assets don't match. And its not easy to fix in my experience
